entity.name: Deepak Ezhumalai
entity.description:
Independent machine-learning researcher in Chennai, India. I work in the open: pre-registered experiments, released code and data, and negative results reported alongside positive ones.

I created and maintain VersionOutcomes (Apache-2.0), the project this application is for.

Other released research software: since November 2026 I have contributed cross-scroll ink detection to ScrollPrize/villa, the MIT-licensed toolkit of the Vesuvius Challenge for reading carbonised Herculaneum scrolls from X-ray CT (pull request ScrollPrize/villa#2512, open). Another participant ran one released checkpoint on one segment from a scroll excluded from that model's training and conversion fitting, and the gain repeated. I also published an analysis of ARC-AGI-3 agent results. Code: https://github.com/DeepakEz

projects.name: VersionOutcomes
projects.description:
VersionOutcomes is an open-source tool that tests whether AI coding models can predict the actual result of a code change, using executable examples from real Python library histories.

It mines every function whose body changed in a library's Git history, runs that function's documentation examples and the calls in the same commit's new regression tests in both the parent and the changed snapshot, and records each call's outcome (return type and value, or exception). A model is shown the before and after source and asked what each version returns and whether the result changed; a scorer compares its answer with the executed outcome.

What exists today (scripts, not yet a packaged command): 16 libraries mined, 1,973 executed outcome pairs, an 82-pair balanced evaluation set, the scorer, every prompt and raw model answer, and results for the five Gemma 4 sizes. On that set Gemma 4 12B detected 31 of 42 real changes with two false alarms but predicted the new outcome for only 19 of the 42. Any reported number can be recomputed from the saved answers.

Limits, stated plainly: published in November 2026; no outside users yet. Mining executes third-party library code and needs a sandbox. The evaluation set is small and Python-only.

plans.name: Maintainer time, six months
plans.description:
Rs 40,000 per month for six months of part-time work (about 20 hours a week, roughly Rs 460 an hour) on VersionOutcomes, paid in quarterly tranches.

From month 1: recruit and support a few independent Python maintainers as pilot users, and record where the tool helps them and where it fails. I can commit to recruiting and supporting them, not to their adoption.
Months 1-2: package the existing scripts into one documented command (mine, execute, build the evaluation set, query a model, score); publish reproducible pilot examples and a catalogue of failure cases.
Months 3-4: extend to a set of additional libraries fixed and published before mining, with executable before/after verification and checks for duplicate cases and ambiguous outputs; report the cost per validated case.
Months 5-6: fix the usability problems pilot users hit, publish what they found useful or not, and publish reproducible model comparisons.

Each quarter: one public engagement (a FOSS United forum update, a blog post or, subject to organiser availability, a meetup talk).

Other funding, disclosed: I have applied for a Sentient Foundation grant and Snorkel Open Benchmarks support (in kind) for this project, OpenAI research credits for a study that uses it, and entered the paper in a Kaggle paper-track competition. All are undecided and contingent. I will disclose any award received during this project and agree budget changes with FOSS United so that no expense is charged twice.

plans.name: Model-evaluation compute (usage budget)
plans.description: Ceiling of Rs 20,000 for up to 100 rented GPU-hours or equivalent API credits, for open models too large for my local GPU or free Kaggle GPUs. Basis: four Gemma 4 sizes on the 82-pair set took about 1.4 hours on one free Kaggle T4 x2 session; the expanded set and more models need an estimated 50-100 GPU-hours. Usage is logged and reported each quarter; unused funds will be returned or reallocated with FOSS United's agreement. No hosting cost: code and data are on GitHub.
